caption: Average Change in INC score from combined layer to base layer, where a negative score means the base layer was better than the combined one and vice versa. The gray and orange bars indicate whether the input to the compression layer is inferred frames or lexical signal, respectively. In all cases, inferred frames has a better effect on base layer and lexical signal has improved combined layer's performance.

annotations.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the average change using compression in relation to observation probability across two categories. The horizontal axis represents "Observation Probability", with values ranging from 0.2 to 0.9, with intervals at 0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9. The vertical axis shows the "Average Change Using Compression", with a linear scale ranging from -3 to 3 in intervals of 1. The chart contains grouped bars for each observation probability value, with each group featuring two bars representing "Inferred Frames" in gray and "Lexical Signal" in yellow. The values of the bars vary within each group, with some positive and some negative. For instance, at an observation probability of 0.2, the "Inferred Frames" bar shows a negative value of -3, while the "Lexical Signal" bar shows a value just below 0. At 0.5, bars have values just below -2 and just above 2. There is no specific sorting of the bars beyond the order of the observation probabilities, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond the use of color differentiation. All the gray bars are below 0, whereas the yellow bar except at 0.2, remain positive. A legend is given at the bottom.
